body.statement: Can \(\widehat\Phi_n\) yield a multiplicity-calibrated test with asymptotically controlled familywise type-I error over rank-degenerate \(q\)-state models and acceptance probability tending uniformly to one when \(\min_{a,k,u}|d_{a,k,u}|\ge\kappa\) and \(\sigma_{q^K}(T_{12})\ge\kappa\) for fixed \(\kappa>0\)?
body.justification: Population zero-versus-nonzero decisions need calibrated separation before deployment.
body.gap: Gu et al. (2018) test provisional \(Q\)-matrix fit, while \(\texttt{cdmTools}\) checks binary structural criteria; neither handles adaptive categorical local-minor queries.
body.consumer: The routine can extend \(\texttt{cdmTools::is.Qid}\) with multiplicity-adjusted uncertainty and a failing-minor trace.
